DestroyTheEvidence.def: Someone who seems not to be directly involved in a crime destroys or hides some evidence relating to it.

DiabolusExMachina.name: Diabolus ex Machina
DiabolusExMachina.def: A plot device that gets the heroes into danger.

DisappointingLastLevel.name: Disappointing Last Level
DisappointingLastLevel.def: The final level of the video game turns out to be very anticlimactic or boing.

DistantFinale.name: Distant Finale
DistantFinale.def: The story ends after a Time Skip with the characters much older.

DoNotSpoilThisEnding.name: Do Not Spoil This Ending
DoNotSpoilThisEnding.def: Producers asking audiences not to spoil the Twist Ending to a work.

DoomedRebellion.name: Doomed Rebellion
DoomedRebellion.def: A story about a character going against society ends with society getting the last laugh.

DoorClosesEnding.name: Door-Closes Ending
DoorClosesEnding.def: The door closes right before the story ends.

DownerEnding.name: Downer Ending
DownerEnding.def: The story ends on a tragic note.

DramaBombFinale.name: Drama Bomb Finale
DramaBombFinale.def: An otherwise comedic story trying its hand at a dramatic moment near the show's last episode or two, totally out of left field.

DumpThemAll.name: Dump Them All
DumpThemAll.def: The lead chooses not to be with any of their prospective Love Interests .

EarnYourBadEnding.name: Earn Your Bad Ending
EarnYourBadEnding.def: A video game where it's more difficult to get the bad ending than the good ending.

EarnYourHappyEnding.name: Earn Your Happy Ending
EarnYourHappyEnding.def: The character doesn't get their happy ending until after enduring a lot of suffering.

TheEnd.name: The End
TheEnd.def: The story ends with a title card reading "The End".

EndGameResultsScreen.name: End-Game Results Screen
EndGameResultsScreen.def: A special screen at game's end that judges your overall performance.

EndingAfterTheEndOfTheWorld.name: Ending After the End of the World
EndingAfterTheEndOfTheWorld.def: The story concludes with an epilogue set after an apocalypse of some form.

TheEndingChangesEverything.name: The Ending Changes Everything
TheEndingChangesEverything.def: A twist ending that changes the very nature of the story.

EndingFatigue.name: Ending Fatigue
EndingFatigue.def: When a work drags on after it should have just ended.

EndingMemorialService.name: Ending Memorial Service
EndingMemorialService.def: The story ends with a funeral.

EndingWithAScream.name: Ending with a Scream
EndingWithAScream.def: The story ends with a character screaming or shouting - in rage, pain, grief, horror, or some other emotion.

EndingTheme.name: Ending Theme
EndingTheme.def: A certain tune that plays at the end of all or most episodes.

EndIsNighEnding.name: "End Is Nigh" Ending
EndIsNighEnding.def: An apocalyptic event is taking place at the very end of the world, but we don't get to see because before the events happen, we're shown the credits.

EndOfEpisodeSilliness.name: End-of-Episode Silliness
EndOfEpisodeSilliness.def: An episode ends with a humorous scene or random bit of dialogue.

EndOfSeriesAwareness.name: End-of-Series Awareness
EndOfSeriesAwareness.def: The ending of the series has the characters acknowledge in-universe that their show is over.

TheEndOfTheBeginning.name: The End of the Beginning
TheEndOfTheBeginning.def: The end of the story is the beginning of a new era.

EndOfTheWorldSpecial.name: "End of the World" Special
EndOfTheWorldSpecial.def: A character is given the power to recreate the whole world.

TheEndOrIsIt.name: The End... Or Is It?
TheEndOrIsIt.def: An ending that casts doubt on the heroes' victory (thus creating a Sequel Hook ).

EndsWithASmile.name: Ends with a Smile
EndsWithASmile.def: Any story (whether an episode or a full-scale work) ends with a character or characters smiling.

EpilogueLetter.name: Epilogue Letter
EpilogueLetter.def: A series ends with the narration of a letter.

EqualizingTheInterspeciesRomance.name: Equalizing the Interspecies Romance
EqualizingTheInterspeciesRomance.def: The story ends with one of the characters in an Interspecies Relationship becoming the other's species.

EverybodyDidIt.name: Everybody Did It
EverybodyDidIt.def: The mystery ends with every suspect guilty.

EverybodyDiesEnding.name: "Everybody Dies" Ending
EverybodyDiesEnding.def: The story ends with everyone killed.

EverybodyHelpsOutDenouement.name: "Everybody Helps Out" Denouement
EverybodyHelpsOutDenouement.def: The story ends with all the characters coming together to help people out.

EverybodyLaughsEnding.name: "Everybody Laughs" Ending
EverybodyLaughsEnding.def: The story ends with everyone laughing.

EverybodyLives.name: Everybody Lives
EverybodyLives.def: The story ends with no one dying.

EveryEpisodeEnding.name: Every Episode Ending
EveryEpisodeEnding.def: A recurring element that concludes each episode/entry of a series.

EveryoneComesBackFantasyPartyEnding.name: "Everyone Comes Back" Fantasy Party Ending
EveryoneComesBackFantasyPartyEnding.def: A fantasy sequence where everyone who previously appeared comes back for a party.

EveryoneJoinTheParty.name: Everyone Join the Party
EveryoneJoinTheParty.def: Random people join the hero or the villain for the final battle.

EverythingExplodesEnding.name: "Everything Explodes" Ending
EverythingExplodesEnding.def: An explosion is used as the final punchline.

ExitPursuedByABear.name: Exit, Pursued by a Bear
ExitPursuedByABear.def: The story ends with the villain being chased by a creature that intends to harm them.

FactionSpecificEndings.name: Faction-Specific Endings
FactionSpecificEndings.def: Each major faction in the game gets an ending where it wins.

FailureGambit.name: Failure Gambit
FailureGambit.def: Failing intentionally as part of a grander scheme.

FakeOutFadeOut.name: Fake-Out Fade-Out
FakeOutFadeOut.def: The show fades out as if it were about to end, but then jumps back in to continue the story.

FakeOutTwist.name: Fake-Out Twist
FakeOutTwist.def: There are two ending plot reveals, the second of which changes the meaning of the first.

FantasyKeepsake.name: Fantasy Keepsake
FantasyKeepsake.def: Someone wakes up, thinking the whole adventure was All Just a Dream , only to find an item proving the adventure was real.

FastForwardToReunion.name: Fast-Forward to Reunion
FastForwardToReunion.def: The main plot resolves with characters going separate ways, the ending skips to future to when they eventually reunite.

TheFellowshipHasEnded.name: The Fellowship Has Ended
TheFellowshipHasEnded.def: The work ends with the main group of protagonists going their separate ways.

FinaleMovie.name: Finale Movie
FinaleMovie.def: A work that isn't a film series receives a conclusion in the form of a feature-length film.

FinaleProductionUpgrade.name: Finale Production Upgrade
FinaleProductionUpgrade.def: When media, at the end of its run, goes all-out on the production value and effort for costumes, characters, guest stars, sets, technology, and depth of a story, or in the additional case of reality TV, real-life competition.

FinaleSeason.name: Finale Season
FinaleSeason.def: When the final season is essentially a long multi-part Grand Finale to the series.

FinalExamFinale.name: Final Exam Finale
FinalExamFinale.def: The finale tries to incorporate all the events that occurred before it.

FinalGirl.name: Final Girl
FinalGirl.def: A female character who survives the events of the story after everyone else dies.

FirstTimeInTheSun.name: First Time in the Sun
FirstTimeInTheSun.def: A character who has lived in seclusion their whole life experiences sunlight the outdoors for the first time.

FissionMailed.name: Fission Mailed
FissionMailed.def: A video game pretends that it's Game Over when it really isn't.

FlyAtTheCameraEnding.name: Fly-at-the-Camera Ending
FlyAtTheCameraEnding.def: The movie ends with a character or object flying straight at the camera.

FocusGroupEnding.name: Focus Group Ending
FocusGroupEnding.def: A work's ending is changed at the last minute after a negative response from the test audience.

FoodEnd.name: Food End
FoodEnd.def: Work ends by showing characters eating.

ForgottenFramingDevice.name: Forgotten Framing Device
ForgottenFramingDevice.def: A story that begins with a Framing Device doesn't include it in the ending.

FourthWallFarewell.name: Fourth Wall Farewell
FourthWallFarewell.def: The final moments of a work involve a sudden breaking of the fourth wall .

FreezeFrameEnding.name: Freeze-Frame Ending
FreezeFrameEnding.def: The ending has the scene freeze with the characters shown ceasing to move.

GainaxEnding.name: Gainax Ending
GainaxEnding.def: The ending is bizarre and incomprehensible, probably due to the budget disappearing.

GeckoEnding.name: Gecko Ending
GeckoEnding.def: An ending of an adaptation that cleans up all the loose ends of the unfinished original.

GhostReunionEnding.name: Ghost Reunion Ending
GhostReunionEnding.def: Dead characters come back in the ending as ghosts.

GoldenEnding.name: Golden Ending
GoldenEnding.def: The best outcome among Multiple Endings .

TheGoodGuysAlwaysWin.name: The Good Guys Always Win
TheGoodGuysAlwaysWin.def: The heroes always succeed in defeating the bad guys.

GoToSleepEnding.name: Go-to-Sleep Ending
GoToSleepEnding.def: The story ends with one or more characters asleep.

GraduateFromTheStory.name: Graduate from the Story
GraduateFromTheStory.def: The main cast of a school-centered story graduate at the ending.

GraduationForEveryone.name: Graduation for Everyone
GraduationForEveryone.def: The whole cast of a show graduate school whether they were a good student or not.

GroupPictureEnding.name: Group Picture Ending
GroupPictureEnding.def: The story closes on a still picture of the main cast.

HappilyEverAfter.name: Happily Ever After
HappilyEverAfter.def: The story ends, the main couple get together, everyone is happy.

HappilyEverBefore.name: Happily Ever Before
HappilyEverBefore.def: An adaptation of a story with a Downer Ending ends on a happy note by ending the story before things get tragic.

HappyEnding.name: Happy Ending
HappyEnding.def: The story ends with nothing bad happening.

HatAndCoatShot.name: Hat-and-Coat Shot
HatAndCoatShot.def: The last shot of a movie clearly indicates this is the ending.

HereWeGoAgain.name: Here We Go Again!
HereWeGoAgain.def: The story ends with the conflict repeating or the characters going through a conflict similar to what they've already been through.

TheHeroDies.name: The Hero Dies
TheHeroDies.def: The protagonist dies at the end of the story.

HisStoryRepeatsItself.name: His Story Repeats Itself
HisStoryRepeatsItself.def: To resolve or come to closure with something that happened in their backstory, a character experiences an event very similar to what happened before.

HomeSweetHome.name: Home Sweet Home
HomeSweetHome.def: A character settles down at home after a long adventure.

HopeSpringsEternal.name: Hope Springs Eternal
HopeSpringsEternal.def: Even if the villain has the upper hand, there's still hope.

HopeSproutsEternal.name: Hope Sprouts Eternal
HopeSproutsEternal.def: A small sprout growing from the ground gives up that things will eventually be better.

HospitalEpilogue.name: Hospital Epilogue
HospitalEpilogue.def: The story ends with a character waking up in a hospital bed.

HowDidWeGetBackHome.name: How Did We Get Back Home?
HowDidWeGetBackHome.def: Transporting the main characters back to their home without giving an explanation.

HumiliationConga.name: Humiliation Conga
HumiliationConga.def: The ending has the villain get his comeuppance by being subjected to a string of embarrassing misfortunes.

IChooseToStay.name: I Choose to Stay
IChooseToStay.def: A character has the chance to go home, but decides to stay where they are now instead.

InfiniteIllusionEnding.name: Infinite Illusion Ending
InfiniteIllusionEnding.def: The story ends with the characters in a dreamworld, unable or unwilling to awake

InferredHolocaust.name: Inferred Holocaust
InferredHolocaust.def: The work glosses over the fact that certain actions and events in the story have most likely resulted in countless deaths.

InterruptedByTheEnd.name: Interrupted by the End
InterruptedByTheEnd.def: The characters are about to do something, but are interrupted by the end of the episode, often in the form of a " The End " card.

IrisOut.name: Iris Out
IrisOut.def: The episode ends with the screen closing in on a character or object.

IShouldWriteABookAboutThis.name: I Should Write a Book About This
IShouldWriteABookAboutThis.def: A story ends with the hero deciding to write a book about their adventures, with the implication that is the story you just heard.

ItAllEndsInTears.name: It All Ends in Tears
ItAllEndsInTears.def: A work ends with a character or characters crying.

JokeEnding.name: Joke Ending
JokeEnding.def: An ending in a game with Multiple Endings that is deliberately sillier and more nonsensical to a substantially large degree than the other endings.

JustLeaveEnding.name: "Just Leave" Ending
JustLeaveEnding.def: A video game gives you the chance to ditch the story.

JokerImmunityWarranty.name: Joker Immunity Warranty
JokerImmunityWarranty.def: A villain who has a tendency to repeatedly survive getting killed ends up dying for real and staying deceased, which is likely to happen to them at the conclusion of the series since having them get killed for good with no further resurrections would effectively end their villainy permanently.

KarmaHoudiniWarranty.name: Karma Houdini Warranty
KarmaHoudiniWarranty.def: A character who tends to get away with their misdeeds finally gets punished for them. Like Joker Immunity Warranty , this is likely to be the result of the series ending and therefore having little reason for the villain to continue evading punishment for their crimes.

KillerFinale.name: Killer Finale
KillerFinale.def: The final installment kills off at least one main character.

LastDayOfSchoolPlot.name: "Last Day of School" Plot
LastDayOfSchoolPlot.def: The characters celebrate their last day of the school year.

LastEpisodeNewCharacter.name: Last Episode, New Character
LastEpisodeNewCharacter.def: The series has a new character introduced in the last episode or installment.

LastEpisodeThemeReprise.name: Last Episode Theme Reprise
LastEpisodeThemeReprise.def: The show's theme song plays towards the end of the last episode.

LastMomentTogether.name: Last Moment Together
LastMomentTogether.def: Two people (friends, family, or lovers) are together for what they know is the final time.

LastSecondEndingChoice.name: Last-Second Ending Choice
LastSecondEndingChoice.def: The ending is determined entirely by a single choice near the end of the game.

LastSecondJokeProblem.name: Last-Second Joke Problem
LastSecondJokeProblem.def: A new problem suddenly appears at the end of a story just to be funny.

LastStand.name: Last Stand
LastStand.def: Someone kills as many enemies as they can before they die.

LastVillainStand.name: Last Villain Stand
LastVillainStand.def: The villain makes a final attempt to beat the heroes.

LeavingYouToFindMyself.name: Leaving You to Find Myself
LeavingYouToFindMyself.def: A character is changing intellectually and dumps their partner to live a new life.

LeftHanging.name: Left Hanging
LeftHanging.def: A series ends with some serious plot threads left unresolved.

LetOffByTheDetective.name: Let Off by the Detective
LetOffByTheDetective.def: The detective figures out who committed a crime, but lets them off because they sympathize with their motive.

LetThePastBurn.name: Let the Past Burn
LetThePastBurn.def: The story ends with a fire destroying the house, along with all it represents.

MaybeEverAfter.name: Maybe Ever After
MaybeEverAfter.def: The story ends by leaving it ambiguous whether the love interests will actually be a couple in the end.

MayItNeverHappenAgain.name: May It Never Happen Again
MayItNeverHappenAgain.def: The story ends with one or more characters ensuring the events won't repeat.

MeaninglessVillainVictory.name: Meaningless Villain Victory
MeaninglessVillainVictory.def: The villain wins, but circumstances make it so that their victory doesn't truly benefit them or is easily overturned by the heroes.

MedalsForEveryone.name: Medals for Everyone
MedalsForEveryone.def: The story ends with the character being awarded for their heroic actions.

MergedReality.name: Merged Reality
MergedReality.def: Saving the day by merging an alternate universe with the normal one.

ModularEpilogue.name: Modular Epilogue
ModularEpilogue.def: Not a continuous ending cutscene, but a sequence of short scenes that show the consequences of your choices.

MovingAwayEnding.name: Moving-Away Ending
MovingAwayEnding.def: The story ends with the characters moving to another area.

MustLetThemGetAway.name: Must Let Them Get Away
MustLetThemGetAway.def: The Hero sees the bad guy escaping, but can't go after him.

NestedStoryReveal.name: Nested Story Reveal
NestedStoryReveal.def: Supposedly real events turn out to be a fictional story within a larger story.

NetworkFinale.name: Network Finale
NetworkFinale.def: When a network decides to go out with a bang just before its Network Death .

NoEnding.name: No Ending
NoEnding.def: The story ends with no resolution.

NoMacGuffinNoWinner.name: No MacGuffin, No Winner
NoMacGuffinNoWinner.def: The story ends with no one getting the MacGuffin .

NonstandardGameOver.name: Non-Standard Game Over
NonstandardGameOver.def: Losing the game at a certain point or in a certain way triggers an exclusive cutscene.

NoRomanticResolution.name: No Romantic Resolution
NoRomanticResolution.def: A romance arc ends without anyone getting together.

NotHisSled.name: Not His Sled
NotHisSled.def: An adaptation changes the well-known ending of the original.

NotQuiteBackToNormal.name: Not Quite Back to Normal
NotQuiteBackToNormal.def: A transformed character retains some residual effects even after reverting back to normal.

NowDoItAgainBackwards.name: Now Do It Again, Backwards
NowDoItAgainBackwards.def: Fixing the problem by doing the same thing in reverse.

NowWhat.name: Now What?
NowWhat.def: The premise is resolved without a satisfying conclusion.

OfferingAHand.name: Offering a Hand
OfferingAHand.def: Before any kind of gesture can be accepted or rejected, someone must first extend a hand.

OfficialKiss.name: Official Kiss
OfficialKiss.def: Two characters kiss, signaling a Relationship Upgrade .

OffIntoTheDistanceEnding.name: Off-into-the-Distance Ending
OffIntoTheDistanceEnding.def: The story ends with The Protagonist traveling into the distance.

OffscreenInertia.name: Offscreen Inertia
OffscreenInertia.def: As long as a character is offscreen, it's assumed that they continue doing whatever it was we last saw them doing.

OhCisco.name: Oh, Cisco!
OhCisco.def: The characters deliver one last joke before the end of the show.

OmegaEnding.name: Omega Ending
OmegaEnding.def: The player must find all other endings to view this one.

OneLastFieldTrip.name: One Last Field Trip
OneLastFieldTrip.def: Characters go on one last outing together. Not necessarily in the last episode, but usually marking an ending of some sort.

OnlyTheLeadsGetADownerEnding.name: Only the Leads Get a Downer Ending
OnlyTheLeadsGetADownerEnding.def: The side characters and setting get a happy ending, but the main characters aren't so lucky.

OnlyTheLeadsGetAHappyEnding.name: Only the Leads Get a Happy Ending
OnlyTheLeadsGetAHappyEnding.def: The main characters get a happy ending, but the side characters aren't so lucky.

OnwardsIntoEternityEpilogue.name: "Onwards into Eternity" Epilogue
OnwardsIntoEternityEpilogue.def: The story ends with an immortal character starting or continuing their lives, with emphasis on the fact that they'll do it forever...

OnTheNext.name: On the Next
OnTheNext.def: Every episode ends with a sneak peek at the next episode.

OrWasItADream.name: Or Was It a Dream?
OrWasItADream.def: It appears that the protagonist only dreamed it , but then it's hinted that what they dreamed had actually happened.

PanUpToTheSkyEnding.name: "Pan Up to the Sky" Ending
PanUpToTheSkyEnding.def: The work ends with the camera panning up to the sky.

PhilosophicalChoiceEndings.name: Philosophical Choice Endings
PhilosophicalChoiceEndings.def: The ending choice lets the player take a stand on a philosophical or ethical issue.

PhotoMemento.name: Photo Memento
PhotoMemento.def: Group of (heroic) characters celebrate the end/importance of an event by posing together for a photograph as a piece of history.

PlayableEpilogue.name: Playable Epilogue
PlayableEpilogue.def: The player is given a degree of control over the ending "cutscene".

PostClimaxConfrontation.name: Post-Climax Confrontation
PostClimaxConfrontation.def: At the very least one of the protagonists faces down one final enemy before the story is truly resolved.

PostFinalBoss.name: Post-Final Boss
PostFinalBoss.def: An easy boss fought after the final boss to wrap up the game's story.

PostFinalLevel.name: Post-Final Level
PostFinalLevel.def: An extremely short level that houses the Final Boss and comes after the actual final level.

PreApocalypticConclusion.name: Pre-Apocalyptic Conclusion
PreApocalypticConclusion.def: The story ends Just Before the End , with no way to stop the apocalypse.

PreEndingCredits.name: Pre-Ending Credits
PreEndingCredits.def: Credits that are displayed... just when the climax is about to take place.

PutOnAPrisonBus.name: Put on a Prison Bus
PutOnAPrisonBus.def: Someone's arrest marks their final appearance in the story. Typically happens near the end of the story.

PyrrhicVictory.name: Pyrrhic Victory
PyrrhicVictory.def: While the characters have won, their victory comes at a price that renders their victory worthless in the end.

QuitAtTheTop.name: Quit at the Top
QuitAtTheTop.def: A character, having reached the pinnacle of their chosen profession, chooses that moment to retire from it.

RailroadToHorizon.name: Railroad to Horizon
RailroadToHorizon.def: A railroad disappearing into the distance is used as a metaphor for the journey ahead.

RayOfHopeEnding.name: "Ray of Hope" Ending
RayOfHopeEnding.def: An ending that would normally be a Downer Ending , but shows that there's still hope left for the heroes.

RefusingParadise.name: Refusing Paradise
RefusingParadise.def: A dead character chooses resurrection over going to a peaceful afterlife.

ResetButtonEnding.name: Reset Button Ending
ResetButtonEnding.def: It looks like the main conflict has been solved, but at the end, something happens that resets the status quo and makes it so it hasn't.

TheResolutionWillNotBeIdentified.name: The Resolution Will Not Be Identified
TheResolutionWillNotBeIdentified.def: An episode of a series that is meant to be the final episode, but is not advertised as such.

RevisedEnding.name: Revised Ending
RevisedEnding.def: The ending is changed for the final product.

RidingIntoTheSunset.name: Riding into the Sunset
RidingIntoTheSunset.def: Character goes off into the distance while the sun is setting.

RocksFallEveryoneDies.name: Rocks Fall, Everyone Dies
RocksFallEveryoneDies.def: The game master of an RPG gets fed up and kills everyone in the game.

RolePlayingEndgame.name: Role-Playing Endgame
RolePlayingEndgame.def: When a Tabletop RPG includes explicit rules for retiring player characters or even for ending the entire campaign.

TheRuinsICaused.name: The Ruins I Caused
TheRuinsICaused.def: After a big, property-damage-causing event, the main characters are seen on a cliff or plateau overlooking the ruins that resulted.

RunningGagged.name: Running Gagged
RunningGagged.def: A recurring gag is used one last time before being retired for good. While this can happen while the show continues production, shows will often choose to retire a particular gag during the final episode.

SaveTheDayTurnAway.name: Save the Day, Turn Away
SaveTheDayTurnAway.def: Someone saves the day but has to dump their love interest.

SaveTheWorldClimax.name: "Save the World" Climax
SaveTheWorldClimax.def: A plot that initially wasn't about saving the world is so by the end.

SavingTheWorldWithArt.name: Saving the World with Art
SavingTheWorldWithArt.def: A character uses a form of art in order to solve a problem or save the world.

SealedWithAKiss.name: Sealed with a Kiss
SealedWithAKiss.def: The Official Couple gets The Big Damn Kiss near or at the end of the story.

SecondChapterCliffhanger.name: Second Chapter Cliffhanger
SecondChapterCliffhanger.def: The second installment of a trilogy ends on a Cliffhanger with several Plot Threads still unresolved.

SecretExpandedEpilogue.name: Secret Expanded Epilogue
SecretExpandedEpilogue.def: In a video game, an extended version of the ending only unlocked by achieving certain conditions.

SequelHook.name: Sequel Hook
SequelHook.def: The ending teases toward a sequel coming up.

SeriesFauxnale.name: Series Fauxnale
SeriesFauxnale.def: An episode of the series looks like the ending due to having clear signs of bringing the story to a definitive conclusion, but it's not the actual finale because the series isn't over just yet.

ShaveAndAHaircut.name: Shave and a Haircut
ShaveAndAHaircut.def: A common musical sting with a five-and-two beat pattern.

ShockAndSwitchEnding.name: Shock-and-Switch Ending
ShockAndSwitchEnding.def: It looks like it's headed for a Sudden Downer Ending , but nope! Everything is fine!

ShootTheShaggyDog.name: Shoot the Shaggy Dog
ShootTheShaggyDog.def: The story ends with the protagonist dying and rubs salt in the wound by revealing their efforts to be pointless.

ShutUpHannibal.name: Shut Up, Hannibal!
ShutUpHannibal.def: The hero gives a defiant response to the villain mocking the hero's idealism or the villain justifying their immoral actions.

SigningOffCatchPhrase.name: Signing-Off Catchphrase
SigningOffCatchPhrase.def: A line of dialog that serves as an Every Episode Ending , usually a way of saying goodbye to the audience.

SnicketWarningLabel.name: Snicket Warning Label
SnicketWarningLabel.def: A warning to stop viewing a work of fiction while it still looks like a happy ending.

SolemnEndingTheme.name: Solemn Ending Theme
SolemnEndingTheme.def: An Ending Theme that sounds wistful.

SomeoneToRememberHimBy.name: Someone to Remember Him By
SomeoneToRememberHimBy.def: A woman turns out to be pregnant with the child of her recently deceased lover.

SomethingWeForgot.name: Something We Forgot
SomethingWeForgot.def: The characters go about their business before we're shown, or they remember, a matter they neglected to take care of.

SoOnceAgainTheDayIsSaved.name: So Once Again, the Day Is Saved
SoOnceAgainTheDayIsSaved.def: A narration placed at the end of every episode to remind the viewers what they just watched.

SoWhatDoWeDoNow.name: So What Do We Do Now?
SoWhatDoWeDoNow.def: A character has just finished an exciting adventure, but finds their now normal life boring.

StandardHeroReward.name: Standard Hero Reward
StandardHeroReward.def: After saving the day, The Hero is rewarded with marriage to a princess.

TheStinger.name: The Stinger
TheStinger.def: A scene that plays after the credits.

StockSeriesFinales.name: Stock Series Finales
StockSeriesFinales.def: Common plots often used in final episodes of shows.

StockSitcomGrandFinale.name: Stock Sitcom Grand Finale
StockSitcomGrandFinale.def: Common plots for ending a situation comedy series.

StopTheHeroTwist.name: "Stop the Hero" Twist
StopTheHeroTwist.def: Not necessarily limited to the ending itself, but the outcome of this twist greatly affects it.

StormingTheCastle.name: Storming the Castle
StormingTheCastle.def: Assaulting the Big Bad's home base.

TheStoryThatNeverWas.name: The Story That Never Was
TheStoryThatNeverWas.def: The solution to the story's conflict is to completely undo the events via Cosmic Retcon .

StrangerInAFamiliarLand.name: Stranger in a Familiar Land
StrangerInAFamiliarLand.def: The hero returns home, but their home has changed so much that it's no longer the same place it was when they originally left.

SuddenDownerEnding.name: Sudden Downer Ending
SuddenDownerEnding.def: The story abruptly ends on a bleak note.

SuddenMusicalEnding.name: Sudden Musical Ending
SuddenMusicalEnding.def: The work or episode ends with a song despite it not being a musical.

SupportingCharactersSayGoodbye.name: Supporting Characters Say Goodbye
SupportingCharactersSayGoodbye.def: The finale includes the protagonist saying good-bye to other characters.

SurpriseParty.name: Surprise Party
SurpriseParty.def: A surprise party is held to celebrate an occasion.

SurprisinglyHappyEnding.name: Surprisingly Happy Ending
SurprisinglyHappyEnding.def: You have braced for a Bittersweet Ending , but things turned out a lot better than you expected.

TakeCareOfTheKids.name: Take Care of the Kids
TakeCareOfTheKids.def: Someone is dying and asks another person to take care of a person (usually a kid as kids are more likely to need care).

TakeMyHand.name: Take My Hand!
TakeMyHand.def: One character is about to fall off a cliff and another tries to catch their hand.

TakenDuringTheEnding.name: Taken During the Ending
TakenDuringTheEnding.def: A character/object is taken away at the end of the story for a purpose, leaving it ambiguous on what's going to happen next.

ThatsAllFolks.name: That's All, Folks!
ThatsAllFolks.def: A character lets the viewer know that it's the end.

ToBeContinuedRightNow.name: To Be Continued... Right Now
ToBeContinuedRightNow.def: Continuing the story immediately after a fake-out of claiming the story will be continued in the next installment.

TorchTheFranchiseAndRun.name: Torch the Franchise and Run
TorchTheFranchiseAndRun.def: The creator(s) deliberately make it so that the work ends in a way that it's impossible to continue the story any further, often by destroying the characters and setting to such a degree that continuations aren't viable due to there being nothing left for future writers and creators to use.

TransformedEverAfter.name: Transformed Ever After
TransformedEverAfter.def: The story ends with a character being permanently transformed - or remaining that way.

TrashTheSet.name: Trash the Set
TrashTheSet.def: The story ends with a regular location in the series being destroyed.

TraumaButtonEnding.name: Trauma Button Ending
TraumaButtonEnding.def: A character has a reaction to a trigger that has to do with events that they just went through.

TrippyFinaleSyndrome.name: Trippy Finale Syndrome
TrippyFinaleSyndrome.def: The finale takes place in some trippy and abstract realm.

TriumphantReprise.name: Triumphant Reprise
TriumphantReprise.def: A tragic song in a musical production gets a more optimistic and triumphant reprise later on. In many cases, the song's brighter counterpart is sung at the ending to further emphasize the protagonist's victory in overcoming the conflict.

TropicalEpilogue.name: Tropical Epilogue
TropicalEpilogue.def: The final shot of the work is the characters on a tropical vacation.

TwoDunIt.name: Two Dun It
TwoDunIt.def: A reveal where two people are responsible for a crime.

UnendingEndCard.name: Unending End Card
UnendingEndCard.def: The game ends on an inescapable congratulatory screen.

UsurpingTheAlphaBitch.name: Usurping the Alpha Bitch
UsurpingTheAlphaBitch.def: The story ends with the new girl overthrowing the Alpha Bitch and taking her place on the social throne.

VelvetRevolution.name: Velvet Revolution
VelvetRevolution.def: The conflict is resolved in peaceful and non-violent revolution.

VictorySex.name: Victory Sex
VictorySex.def: Characters celebrate their victory with sex.

TheVillainMustBePunished.name: The Villain Must Be Punished
TheVillainMustBePunished.def: The villain must pay for their crimes; merely foiling their plans isn't enough.

WasItReallyWorthIt.name: Was It Really Worth It?
WasItReallyWorthIt.def: A character finally succeeds in their goal, but doesn't enjoy their victory because they're ashamed of what they had to do to make it possible.

WealthyEverAfter.name: Wealthy Ever After
WealthyEverAfter.def: The story ends with a character becoming wealthy.

WeddingBellsForSomeoneElse.name: Wedding Bells... for Someone Else
WeddingBellsForSomeoneElse.def: Two people look like they are about to be married, only for it to turn out they're guests at someone else's wedding.

WeddingFinale.name: Wedding Finale
WeddingFinale.def: Someone gets married at the end of the story.

WeddingsForEveryone.name: Weddings for Everyone
WeddingsForEveryone.def: Multiple couples get married at the end of the story.

WhatCliffHanger.name: What Cliff Hanger?
WhatCliffHanger.def: A cliffhanger which merely promises that some shocking plot twist will be revealed later, instead of just revealing it right now, is usually not that exciting.

WhatNowEnding.name: "What Now?" Ending
WhatNowEnding.def: A Cliffhanger that allows time to pass within the show between episodes.

WhereAreTheyNowEpilogue.name: "Where Are They Now?" Epilogue
WhereAreTheyNowEpilogue.def: The ending shows what became of the characters after the events of the story.

WhereItAllBegan.name: Where It All Began
WhereItAllBegan.def: The hero's journey ends the same location where it began.

WillReturnCaption.name: "Will Return" Caption
WillReturnCaption.def: The ending has a caption promising that the main character will return.

AWinnerIsYou.name: A Winner Is You
AWinnerIsYou.def: The video game ends with nothing more than a message congratulating the player for completing the game.

WorldHealingWave.name: World-Healing Wave
WorldHealingWave.def: A wave envelopes the world to heal it from all the damage and corruption.

WrapItUp.name: Wrap It Up
WrapItUp.def: A short-notice Finale for a soon to be cancelled work.

WrapUpSong.name: Wrap-Up Song
WrapUpSong.def: A song that ends every episode.

YeahShot.name: "YEAH!" Shot
YeahShot.def: The final shot of a work freezes on a character jumping in the air with their hands up.

YourPrincessIsInAnotherCastle.name: Your Princess Is in Another Castle!
YourPrincessIsInAnotherCastle.def: An ending that isn't really the end.

AnachronicOrder.name: Anachronic Order
AnachronicOrder.def: Scenes, episodes, or installments are deliberately presented out of chronological order.

AndThatLittleGirlWasMe.name: ...And That Little Girl Was Me
AndThatLittleGirlWasMe.def: A character recounts a story about a seemingly irrelevant person before revealing the story is about themself.

BackToFront.name: Back to Front
BackToFront.def: The story is told backwards, from end to beginning.

CallForward.name: Call-Forward
CallForward.def: The flashback sequence alludes to events that the audience knows eventually happened.

DashedPlotLine.name: Dashed Plot Line
DashedPlotLine.def: Time periods larger than one year where nothing interesting happens are skipped to preserve The Law of Conservation of Detail .

DeathByFlashback.name: Death by Flashback
DeathByFlashback.def: Revealing a character's backstory is a good indication that they are about to die.

DecadeThemedFilter.name: Decade-Themed Filter
DecadeThemedFilter.def: A flashback from a different decade is filtered in the manner of the camera technology of the time.

DelayedNarratorIntroduction.name: Delayed Narrator Introduction
DelayedNarratorIntroduction.def: The narrator is only introduced partway through their own story.

FabulaAndSujet.name: Fabula and Sujet
FabulaAndSujet.def: Distinction between the chronological order of the story's events (Fabula) and the order in which we see the scenes (Sujet).

FlashbackBackBack.name: Flashback... Back... Back...
FlashbackBackBack.def: Flashback is preceded by an echoey sound effect.

FlashbackBPlot.name: Flashback B-Plot
FlashbackBPlot.def: A linear secondary story is told through flashbacks alongside the main story, both involving the same character(s).

FlashbackCut.name: Flashback Cut
FlashbackCut.def: A very brief flashback (usually lasts a few seconds) in the middle of a scene

FlashbackEcho.name: Flashback Echo
FlashbackEcho.def: Events in the present are quickly followed by flashbacks to similar events in the past.

FlashbackEffects.name: Flashback Effects
FlashbackEffects.def: Visual and audio effects used to indicate a flashback.

FlashbackNightmare.name: Flashback Nightmare
FlashbackNightmare.def: A character dreams of a traumatic past event.

FlashbackStares.name: Flashback Stares
FlashbackStares.def: A character stares into the distance while remembering a past event.

FlashbackToCatchphrase.name: Flashback to Catchphrase
FlashbackToCatchphrase.def: A flashback reveals the origin of a character's catchphrase.

FlashbackTwist.name: Flashback Twist
FlashbackTwist.def: A flashback is used and subverts the audience's expectations.

FlashbackWithTheOtherDarrin.name: Flashback with the Other Darrin
FlashbackWithTheOtherDarrin.def: A flashback to a previously shot scene with a new actor .

FlashbackWithinAFlashback.name: Flashback Within a Flashback
FlashbackWithinAFlashback.def: A flashback occurs inside another flashback.

FlashForward.name: Flash Forward
FlashForward.def: A break in the story to show a future plot development ahead of time.

Futureshadowing.name: Futureshadowing
Futureshadowing.def: We see the aftermath of an event before seeing the event itself.

GrownUpsFormerAuthorityFigure.name: Grown-Up's Former Authority Figure
GrownUpsFormerAuthorityFigure.def: An adult runs into a teacher or other authority figure from their childhood.

HappyFlashback.name: Happy Flashback
HappyFlashback.def: A flashback to a happy(er) time in a character's life. Happier Home Movie

HilariousInFlashback.name: Hilarious in Flashback
HilariousInFlashback.def: Events in a flashback turn out to be funny because the audience knows the present state of things.

InstantMysteryJustDeleteScene.name: Instant Mystery: Just Delete Scene!
InstantMysteryJustDeleteScene.def: A scene is skipped so the viewer doesn't know what happened there for the sake of mystery and suspense.

Interquel.name: Interquel
Interquel.def: A work takes place in the middle of a previously-published work (or in between two).

InterrogationFlashback.name: Interrogation Flashback
InterrogationFlashback.def: The story is told via a character being pumped for information.

MonochromePast.name: Monochrome Past
MonochromePast.def: Past events depicted in black and white, sepia tone, or muted colors.

NotTheFirstVictim.name: Not the First Victim
NotTheFirstVictim.def: A predator had victims before the apparent "first" victim.

OffstageWaitingRoom.name: Offstage Waiting Room
OffstageWaitingRoom.def: Some characters do important things for the plot while others wait for them to finish their own adventure (do nothing).

OnceMoreWithClarity.name: Once More, with Clarity
OnceMoreWithClarity.def: We see a scene and it seems to mean one thing; after several plot developments, we see the same scene, and this time it means something completely different.

OriginsEpisode.name: Origins Episode
OriginsEpisode.def: An episode of the series devoted to revealing the origins of an established character, which will often have the character's backstory shown in flashback sequences, or even have the entire episode take place sometime prior to the character's chronological debut.

PensieveFlashback.name: Pensieve Flashback
PensieveFlashback.def: A character physically observes a flashback.

POVSequel.name: P.O.V. Sequel
POVSequel.def: A story retold from another character's perspective.

RecollectionSidequest.name: Recollection Sidequest
RecollectionSidequest.def: A sidequest that involves collecting memories to gain information about prior events.

RetrauxFlashback.name: Retraux Flashback
RetrauxFlashback.def: A flashback is presented with an appropriate Art Shift .

RewatchBonus.name: Rewatch Bonus
RewatchBonus.def: Now that the work is over, we'll find a new meaning in those little strange details if we watch it again.

SeamlessScenery.name: Seamless Scenery
SeamlessScenery.def: Different scenes transition into each other as if they're still in one location or linear sequence; characters can literally walk into the next scene.

SequencingDeception.name: Sequencing Deception
SequencingDeception.def: The work implies that two scenes happen simultaneously or one after the other, but the true order is completely different than we thought.

StylisticCallback.name: Stylistic Callback
StylisticCallback.def: A work references stylistic changes since prior works in the same series.

SuspiciouslySpecificSermon.name: Suspiciously Specific Sermon
SuspiciouslySpecificSermon.def: Religious service is oddly plot relevant.

ThatOneSummer.name: That One Summer
ThatOneSummer.def: Summer is a magnet for the memory.

ThirdPersonFlashback.name: Third-Person Flashback
ThirdPersonFlashback.def: A person remembering a past event will see everything from a third-person perspective instead of through their own eyes (first person).

TimeSkip.name: Time Skip
TimeSkip.def: A good chunk of time is skipped between two plot developments or installments.

TroubledBackstoryFlashback.name: Troubled Backstory Flashback
TroubledBackstoryFlashback.def: Flashback showing the moment a character's life goes downhill.

ViewersAreGoldfish.name: Viewers Are Goldfish
ViewersAreGoldfish.def: The creators think we can't remember past plot developments, so they will remind us constantly.

AscendToAHigherPlaneOfExistence.name: Ascend to a Higher Plane of Existence

BucketList.name: Bucket List
BucketList.def: To do everything on a certain list before one dies.

CallOfTheWildBlueYonder.name: Call of the Wild Blue Yonder

CheatingDamnation.name: Cheating Damnation
CheatingDamnation.def: A character plans to cheat their way out of Hell.

GottaCatchThemAll.name: Gotta Catch Them All
GottaCatchThemAll.def: To collect everything in a set.

MakeWrongWhatOnceWentRight.name: Make Wrong What Once Went Right

RestrainedResistanceRecklessRebellion.name: Restrained Resistance, Reckless Rebellion
RestrainedResistanceRecklessRebellion.def: Various groups share the same goals (e.g. the overthrow of the Evil Overlord or The Empire ) but because of their differing motivations and/or methods they sometimes clash.

Revenge.name: Revenge
Revenge.def: To get back at the one who wronged you.

SaveThisPersonSaveTheWorld.name: Save This Person, Save the World

SmallMindedVillain.name: Small-Minded Villain
SmallMindedVillain.def: A villain who never rises above petty crimes despite their talent and powers.

TheGoodKingdom.name: The Good Kingdom
TheGoodKingdom.def: , for a story in which the Hero must save the world from impending doom, and

Suburbia.name: Suburbia
Suburbia.def: can be either, depending on where the story falls on the Sliding Scale of Idealism Versus Cynicism .

TheHero.name: The Hero
TheHero.def: may be dissatisfied with the ordinary and express a desire for adventure. In musicals this can be expressed through an "I Want" Song or a Wanderlust Song .

HeelFaceRevolvingDoor.name: The Shapeshifter
HeelFaceRevolvingDoor.def: Someone you don't trust but nonetheless need for their capabilities or knowledge.

HerosMuse.name: The Goddess
HerosMuse.def: a figure that serves as inspiration to the hero, often a love interest and/or another heroic figure they admire.

TheVamp.name: The Temptress
TheVamp.def: a figure that tries to derail the journey and/or corrupt the hero.

WellDoneSonGuy.name: Atonement With the Father
WellDoneSonGuy.def: George Lucas loved this step. Oedipus probably didn't. Variants include a final showdown with an Archnemesis Dad (sometimes still ending in atonement if Death Equals Redemption ) and Calling the Old Man Out .

ActionFilmQuietDramaScene.name: Time out just before the big battle
ActionFilmQuietDramaScene.def: The Heroes gather around a campfire and prepare for the battle, tell stories, confess their feelings, etc. It reminds them of what's at stake, and serves as a breather after all the action of the Road of Trials.

ActuallyADoombot.name: Actually a Doombot
ActuallyADoombot.def: The villain the hero was fighting turns out to be a robot double or clone of the real villain.

AssPull.name: Ass Pull
AssPull.def: An explanation or solution that comes out of nowhere and disregards what has already been established by the story, named from the idea that the writer just pulled an answer from their ass in desperation for a quick and convenient way to resolve the conflict.

AwesomeAchievementPettyPurpose.name: Awesome Achievement, Petty Purpose
AwesomeAchievementPettyPurpose.def: Someone's motivation for building a great invention or achieving a difficult goal turns out to be pretty petty.

BaitAudienceSurrogate.name: Bait Audience Surrogate
BaitAudienceSurrogate.def: The relatable blank-slate main character isn't as relatable as we thought.

BookedFullOfMooks.name: Booked Full of Mooks
BookedFullOfMooks.def: A character in a public space discovers that all the bystanders around them are actually another character's employees or co-conspirators.

CanonCharacterAllAlong.name: Canon Character All Along
CanonCharacterAllAlong.def: The adaptation features a character who initially appears to be a completely new character created for the adaptation , but it later turns out that the character is really the adaptation's interpretation of an already established character.

CaptainObviousReveal.name: Captain Obvious Reveal
CaptainObviousReveal.def: A twist that is too easy to figure out before it's revealed.

ChairReveal.name: Chair Reveal
ChairReveal.def: A chair turns around to reveal a surprise occupant.

ConfirmBeforeReveal.name: Confirm Before Reveal
ConfirmBeforeReveal.def: A character asks a quick question about something they're about to reveal before revealing it.

DaydreamSurprise.name: Daydream Surprise
DaydreamSurprise.def: A brief scene is immediately shown to only be a daydream one of the characters is having.

DiedInIgnorance.name: Died in Ignorance
DiedInIgnorance.def: A death occurs before an important revelation that may completely change the context of a scene.

EarthAllAlong.name: Earth All Along
EarthAllAlong.def: What was thought to be an alien planet turns out to really be Earth.

EdibleTreasure.name: Edible Treasure
EdibleTreasure.def: The supposedly valuable treasure turns out to be made of food.

FakeMystery.name: Fake Mystery
FakeMystery.def: The crime turns out to be staged/faked.

FamilyRelationshipSwitcheroo.name: Family Relationship Switcheroo
FamilyRelationshipSwitcheroo.def: A person finds out that their relative was actually related to them in a different way than they originally believed.

FantasyAllAlong.name: Fantasy All Along
FantasyAllAlong.def: It turns out the events were all just part of someone's delusion.

GoodAllAlong.name: Good All Along
GoodAllAlong.def: Someone thought to be evil turns out to be good.

HijackedByGanon.name: Hijacked by Ganon
HijackedByGanon.def: An entry in a series with a new villian has an iconic pre-established villian take over as the main antagonist.

HybridAllAlong.name: Hybrid All Along
HybridAllAlong.def: Someone discovers that they’re a hybrid of multiple species.

IAmNotYourFather.name: I Am Not Your Father
IAmNotYourFather.def: A father reveals to his child that they were adopted.

IMadeCopies.name: I Made Copies
IMadeCopies.def: A character tears up a contract only to be told copies were made.

InsanityEstablishmentScene.name: Insanity Establishment Scene
InsanityEstablishmentScene.def: When a character is revealed to be crazy later instead of from the start.

ItWasWithYouAllAlong.name: It Was with You All Along

TheManBehindTheCurtain.name: The Man Behind the Curtain
TheManBehindTheCurtain.def: An influential and previously unseen Big Bad is revealed to be pathetically weak.

MemoryRestoringMelody.name: Memory-Restoring Melody
MemoryRestoringMelody.def: A crucial plot point is revealed when a character who previously forgot or suppressed it listens to a certain song.

MidSeasonTwist.name: Mid-Season Twist
MidSeasonTwist.def: A major plot twist occurs in the middle of a season of a show.

MonsterSuit.name: Monster Suit
MonsterSuit.def: The monster is actually a person in disguise.

NiceJobBreakingItHero.name: Nice Job Breaking It, Hero!
NiceJobBreakingItHero.def: The hero tries to save the day, but their efforts end up making things worse.

NotQuiteDead.name: Not Quite Dead
NotQuiteDead.def: Someone thought to be dead turns out to be still alive.

NotSoEpisodic.name: Not So Episodic
NotSoEpisodic.def: Early episodes turn out to be connected.

NotSoRemote.name: Not So Remote
NotSoRemote.def: A person thinks they're far from civilization, but ends up discovering they're closer to home than they thought.

NotTooDeadToSaveTheDay.name: Not Too Dead to Save the Day

PhotoDoodleRecognition.name: Photo Doodle Recognition
PhotoDoodleRecognition.def: Recognizing someone by drawing their disguise or distinguishing features on a photograph where they don't have them.

ThePictureCameWithTheFrame.name: The Picture Came with the Frame

PosedCorpseReveal.name: Posed Corpse Reveal
PosedCorpseReveal.def: A dead character is initially mistaken for alive, including by the audience.

PossessedAllAlong.name: Possessed All Along
PossessedAllAlong.def: A character assumed to be acting of their own accord turns out to actually be possessed/mind-controled/ect.

ProppingUpTheirPatsy.name: Propping Up Their Patsy
ProppingUpTheirPatsy.def: A culprit proclaims the innocence of another suspect to conceal their own culpability or further their own agenda.

ProsceniumReveal.name: Proscenium Reveal
ProsceniumReveal.def: The moment when a scene that we're watching—thinking it's an event that's really happening within the world of the story—is revealed to be a part of a Show Within the Show , or some kind of simulation that the characters are involved in.

ReallyRoyaltyReveal.name: Really Royalty Reveal
ReallyRoyaltyReveal.def: Someone who believed themselves to be a peasant or commoner discovers they're actually royalty.

RedeemingReplacement.name: Redeeming Replacement
RedeemingReplacement.def: A villain gets a heroic successor who aims to do good in order to make up for their predecessor's crimes.

ReleasedToElsewhere.name: Released to Elsewhere
ReleasedToElsewhere.def: People are executed and the authorities lie that they were simply relocated to new places.

RoboticReveal.name: Robotic Reveal
RoboticReveal.def: A supposedly organic being turns out to really be a robot.

RoleReversalBoss.name: Role-Reversal Boss
RoleReversalBoss.def: In a game, the player unexpectedly finds themselves controlling a boss character.

SecretTestOfCharacter.name: Secret Test of Character
SecretTestOfCharacter.def: The hero is then told that by forfeiting the challenge in a certain way is exactly what was needed to triumph, and that it was actually a test of character, and they have passed with flying colors.

SerendipityShock.name: Serendipity Shock
SerendipityShock.def: A character suddenly gets the one thing they've always wanted, and is able to keep it permanently.

SurprisinglyMundaneReason.name: Surprisingly Mundane Reason
SurprisinglyMundaneReason.def: The characters believe that another character's actions are for some outlandish/profound reason, only for it to be revealed that they were actually doing as they did for mundane reasons.

SurvivalThroughSelfSacrifice.name: Survival Through Self-Sacrifice
SurvivalThroughSelfSacrifice.def: A character chooses to sacrifice his or her life, and is spared for doing so.

SympatheticWithAddedContext.name: Sympathetic with Added Context
SympatheticWithAddedContext.def: A character seems unsympathetic, but added context reveals that they are.

TakeAThirdOption.name: Take a Third Option
TakeAThirdOption.def: When someone has to decide between two choices, they work around and pick a third choice.

TomatoInTheMirror.name: Tomato in the Mirror
TomatoInTheMirror.def: A character discovers that they are not what they think they are.

TomatoSurprise.name: Tomato Surprise
TomatoSurprise.def: Something is known to the characters in-universe, but is revealed to the audience as a twist.

TwistingTheProphecy.name: Twisting the Prophecy
TwistingTheProphecy.def: Knowingly fulfilling a prophecy in a way that creates a favourable outcome.

UndercoverCopReveal.name: Undercover Cop Reveal
UndercoverCopReveal.def: A person turns out to be an undercover cop.

UnexpectedCharacter.name: Unexpected Character
UnexpectedCharacter.def: The work features a character in the franchise that audiences did not anticipate to be involved.

UnreliableNarrator.name: Unreliable Narrator
UnreliableNarrator.def: It is hinted that the narrator may be exaggerating or glossing over parts of the story, if they weren't just outright lying.

TheUnreveal.name: The Un-Reveal
TheUnreveal.def: Even when it looks like the big secret will be revealed, it never is.

UnsympatheticWithAddedContext.name: Unsympathetic with Added Context
UnsympatheticWithAddedContext.def: A character seems sympathetic, but added context reveals that they aren't.

TheUntwist.name: The Un-Twist
TheUntwist.def: Deliberately setting up a Captain Obvious Reveal while also hinting at a Red Herring , so that the audience is surprised when it's played straight.

WhamEpisode.name: Wham Episode
WhamEpisode.def: An episode that suddenly changes the series' tone from then on. Wham Episode Fallout : An episode where the consequences of the Wham! Episode are shown.

WhamLine.name: Wham Line
WhamLine.def: The mood of the work changes abruptly all because of a single line of dialogue.

WhamSound.name: Wham Sound
WhamSound.def: A specific sound, or music (diegetic or not), radically alters a scene.

WontDoYourDirtyWork.name: Won't Do Your Dirty Work
WontDoYourDirtyWork.def: The hero/villain is told to solve his own problems.

YankTheDogsChain.name: Yank the Dog's Chain
YankTheDogsChain.def: Right when it looks like this unfortunate person will finally have better luck, their chances at happiness are ruined at the last minute.

LoveBeforeFirstSight.name: Love Before First Sight
LoveBeforeFirstSight.def: One or both characters fall in love with their love interest before they even meet. Because Destiny Says So

ReincarnationRomance.name: Reincarnation Romance
ReincarnationRomance.def: The two characters were a couple in their past lives.

InLoveWithTheMark.name: In Love with the Mark
InLoveWithTheMark.def: One character is a hired killer, and the other is the person they're supposed to kill.

LoveAtFirstSight.name: Love at First Sight
LoveAtFirstSight.def: One or both characters fall in love the moment they see the other.

AMatchMadeInStockholm.name: A Match Made in Stockholm
AMatchMadeInStockholm.def: The pair meet when one kidnaps the other.

RescueRomance.name: Rescue Romance
RescueRomance.def: One character is rescuing the other.

JustFriends.name: Just Friends
JustFriends.def: The pair aren't officially a couple yet. Attractiveness Isolation

NotADate.name: Not a Date
NotADate.def: They spend time together, but one or both of them specify that it's not a date.

CannotSpitItOut.name: Cannot Spit It Out
CannotSpitItOut.def: One character tries to confess their love, but can't bring themself to say it. I "Uh" You, Too : ...but other gets the message regardless.

MomentKiller.name: Moment Killer
MomentKiller.def: Someone else ruins a romantic moment between the pair.

RedundantRomanceAttempt.name: Redundant Romance Attempt
RedundantRomanceAttempt.def: Acting out of character to impress a love interest who likes your true personality.

ShipTease.name: Ship Tease
ShipTease.def: The pair have a sweet moment together, hinting at future romance. Caught in the Rain

CantLiveWithThemCantLiveWithoutThem.name: Can't Live With Them, Can't Live Without Them

DidYouThinkICantFeel.name: Did You Think I Can't Feel?

LoveConfession.name: Love Confession
LoveConfession.def: One character confesses their love for the other. Accidental Declaration of Love : ...unintentionally.

LoveConfessor.name: Love Confessor
LoveConfessor.def: A third party tells one character that the other loves them.

LoveEpiphany.name: Love Epiphany
LoveEpiphany.def: One character realizes they're in love with the other. Green-Eyed Epiphany

LoveRevelationEpiphany.name: Love Revelation Epiphany
LoveRevelationEpiphany.def: ...after said other character confesses their own love.

RelationshipLabelingProblems.name: Relationship Labeling Problems
RelationshipLabelingProblems.def: The pair hesitate to call themselves a couple.

RelationshipUpgrade.name: Relationship Upgrade
RelationshipUpgrade.def: Falling-in-Love Montage Literally Falling in Love

FirstKiss.name: First Kiss
FirstKiss.def: The pair finally kiss. The Big Damn Kiss

IDontWantToRuinOurFriendship.name: I Don't Want to Ruin Our Friendship

ItsNotYouItsMyEnemies.name: It's Not You, It's My Enemies

SecondActBreakUp.name: Second-Act Breakup
SecondActBreakUp.def: Break His Heart to Save Him

DowntimeDowngrade.name: Downtime Downgrade
DowntimeDowngrade.def: (where the "Second Act" is either a Sequel or in between episodes )

TheGrovel.name: The Grovel
TheGrovel.def: (may involve an Anguished Declaration of Love )

WhyWouldAnyoneTakeHimBack.name: Why Would Anyone Take Him Back?

BetterAsFriends.name: Better as Friends
BetterAsFriends.def: The pair decide they're happier when they're not a couple.

CleaningUpRomanticLooseEnds.name: Cleaning Up Romantic Loose Ends
CleaningUpRomanticLooseEnds.def: (exit point; do not pass go; do not collect $200 )

IWantMyBelovedToBeHappy.name: I Want My Beloved to Be Happy

HerHeartWillGoOn.name: Her Heart Will Go On
HerHeartWillGoOn.def: (exit point) Someone to Remember Him By

TogetherInDeath.name: Together in Death
TogetherInDeath.def: (exit point) Reincarnation Romance (Go back to start )
